steps.body: A zero in the tens means the ones cannot borrow next door — first break a hundred into tens, THEN break one of those tens into ones.
steps.narration: A zero in the tens means the ones cannot borrow next door — first break a hundred into tens, THEN break one of those tens into ones.

commonBuilds.feedback: That kept all 4 flats — the broken hundred must leave the hundreds place.
Ten rods plus 12 cubes counts the broken ten twice — one rod became those cubes.

widget.missFeedback: That build names a different number — total each unit's worth and match 402 exactly.
widget.successFeedback: 3 flats, 9 rods, 12 cubes still make 402 — the hundred fed the tens, and a ten fed the ones.

predict.prompt: The tens digit is 0 and the ones need help. Where does the value come from?
predict.reveal: The hundred opens into ten tens, and then one of those tens opens into ten ones.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2b across zero.
invariants: Trading between places changes the FORM of a quantity, never its value — the model and the number must stay equal for g2b across zero.
misconceptions: Treating a trade as adding or removing amount instead of renaming the same total.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the blocks stop matching the written number?

commonErrors.feedback: The hundred you opened to feed the zero tens was never taken out of the hundreds.
The ten you broke for the ones still sits whole in the tens place — remove it.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the places up — hundreds with hundreds, tens with tens, ones with ones — and work one column at a time.

explanationVariants: Chained trades are still equal trades.

widget.prompt: While solving with 256, a student trades ten ones for a ten. Why is that allowed?

options.label: Because ten ones and one ten are equal amounts
options.feedback: Correct — the trade is legal exactly because both forms name the same quantity.

options.label: Because the answer gets bigger
options.feedback: A valid trade never changes the total at all — that is the whole point of it.

options.label: Because tens look nicer than ones
options.feedback: Looks are not the reason; equal VALUE is what licenses the swap.

options.label: Because subtraction requires it every time
options.feedback: Many subtractions need no trade; the trade appears only when a place runs short.
